title: lava db:status --json
description: What the migration repository has recorded, what is still on disk unapplied, and what it remembers without a file. Three lists rather than two because the third is the one that bites: an applied migration whose file is gone means the schema carries a change nothing can undo, and `db:rollback` will refuse to go past it.

applied.description: Recorded migrations, oldest first. Read from the repository table, not from the files, so a deleted file still appears here until it is rolled back.

name.description: The migration's file name without .php — the name is the identity, which is why it is also the repository's primary key.

batch.description: The run that applied it. One batch per `db:migrate`, so a batch is 'a deploy'.

applied_at.description: When it was recorded, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in the server's timezone.

pending.description: Migrations on disk the repository has not recorded, in the order they would be applied. Empty when the database is up to date.

orphaned.description: Recorded as applied, but the file is gone. Non-empty here is the warning that `db:rollback` will refuse.

batch.description: The highest batch recorded, or 0 when nothing has ever been applied — which is why it is 0 rather than null on a fresh database.

pending_count.description: count(pending), so a caller does not have to measure the list to branch on it.
